trials.output_text: {"subjective": "The patient reports headaches almost every evening for three weeks. The headaches are described as heavy and pressing at the back of the head and sometimes across the forehead. They are not sharp. Paracetamol helps a little. The headaches are worse when stressed or skipping lunch. Patient experiences occasional blurry vision in the evening, but it clears. No vomiting, blurred vision, flashing lights, or weakness. Patient reports waking up two times per night to urinate and experiencing increased thirst. Patient has lost about 2-3 kg recently. Patient reports tingling/pins and needles sensation in both feet, especially at night, which is getting worse. The patient stopped smoking four years ago and drinks 2-3 beers on Saturdays. Patient takes amlodipine five milligrams once daily (misses it sometimes) and metformin five hundred milligrams twice daily with meals (misses the evening dose). Home blood pressure readings are one fifty over ninety and one forty-eight over ninety-two. Morning blood sugar is around nine to ten, and after meals it is twelve. Patient reports mild ankle swelling in the evenings. The patient eats tea with two spoons of sugar and bread for breakfast, rice or ugali with stew for lunch, fried fish for dinner, and drinks soda almost every day (one to two half-litre sodas). Patient adds a lot of salt to their food. Patient has a family history of diabetes, stroke, and high blood pressure.
